title: Quarterly Services Report (Second Quarter 2026) — the last full report on the PRE-AIES basis, revising the largest quarterly services gain on record (+3.1%), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: CENSUS: four census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, all naming the date. (1) services/release_schedule.html (HTTP 200, 48,030 bytes), the QSS program's OWN schedule table headed "2025/2026 Release Schedule ... All releases occur at 10 am", whose "2026 Quarter 2" row reads "Thursday, August 20, 2026" (advance) and "Wednesday, September 9, 2026" (full report). (2) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "Quarterly Services Survey | September 9, 2026 | 10:00 AM | Second Quarter 2026", release code A202609091000, reference A202602 — parsed alongside six prior-year calendars into 55 services rows 2020-02-19 -> 2026-12-10. (3) The live release itself, services/qss/qss-current.pdf (HTTP 200, 611,965 bytes) = CB26-139, the Q2 2026 advance, whose summary box reads "Next release: September 9, 2026". (4) The SAME release's Release Schedule paragraph, a separate statement in a separate section: "The second quarter 2026 Quarterly Services Report is scheduled for release on September 9, 2026." Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> CENSUS: on the two-primary precedent this calendar already carries for qss-q3-2026-12-10, advance-services-q3-2026-11-19, housing-starts-2026-12-17 and m3-full-report-2026-12-03; four primaries clear it with room. Confirmed is a claim about the SCHEDULED DATE: the full half of this series has never been suspended in 28 scheduled rows 2020-2026 (the advance half has, once), and 2026-09-09 carries no funding-cliff exposure. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-06, D-3) after reading its one proposal, `from-qss-q3-2026-12-10`, which is now shadowed. The proposal's frame — this is the only out-of-sample test of the advance->full revision bound before 12-10 — is SUPPORTED, and three findings sharpen it. (1) THE NUMBER BEING REVISED IS THE LARGEST ON RECORD. CB26-139 prints Q2 2026 Selected Services Total at $6,421.9 billion, +3.1 percent (+/-0.4) q/q and +7.7 percent (+/-0.6) y/y. Across 12 realized SA q/q readings harvested from Census PDFs this session (Q3 2022 -> Q1 2026) the median is +1.75% and the MAXIMUM is +2.4%; +3.1% clears the record high by 0.7pp. The 0.00/0.10/0.20pp revision bound was measured entirely on prints of +0.8% to +2.3%, so 09-09 is out of sample on the INPUT, not just on the date. (2) THE BENCHMARK CHANNEL IS A LEVEL RESTATEMENT AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE LARGER THAN THE HEADLINE REVISION, AND IT HAS ALREADY SLIPPED ONCE ON A FUNDING LAPSE. Routine advance->full level restatements run 0.016-0.132% (n=5, measured here); the March 2023 release carrying the 2021 Service Annual Survey benchmark restated Q3 2022 from $5,064.2B to $4,948.6B (-2.28%) and its SA q/q from +2.2% to +1.9% (0.30pp). CB26-34 and CB26-39 both state verbatim that "due to the lapse in federal funding" the 2023+2024 AIES revisions "will be released at a later date"; CB26-99 and CB26-139 now name the November 2026 advance. So 2026-09-09 is the LAST full report published on the pre-AIES basis. (3) NOTHING READS IT, RE-MEASURED NOT INHERITED. Zero of 3,665 shared strings in the Atlanta Fed's 10.9 MB GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx name the Quarterly Services Survey or the Advance Services Report (71 name CPI/retail sales/housing starts), across 1,871 ContribArchives vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28; PostedUpdates posts NO vintage on 2026-09-09 (nearest 09-03 and 09-10); a re-grep of trade-playbooks.md + multi-symbol-sweep.md returns 0 macro- or services-keyed hits. Impact LOW and symbols empty on those measurements. The corridor: unlike its 12-10 sibling this print does NOT share its session with CPI or PPI — PPI is 09-10 and CPI is 09-11 on two independent primaries (this calendar's confirmed entries and the Atlanta Fed PostedUpdates rows) — but 09-09 belongs to the 10y note auction (high, confirmed) and Apple's iPhone 18 launch, inside the FOMC blackout that opened 09-05. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
